text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- A vote of no confidence against Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi narrowly failed with 45 votes in favour, 46 against, one abstention and four members failing to vote. The vote was backed by opposition parties the Reform Party, the Moderates, Fatherland Union and Right-wing factions but also by the Centre Party faction and two Russian members. The ruling Coalition Party/rural parties and the Development Party opposed it.

- An Estonian-Lithuanian social protection agreement was signed by Foreign Ministers Toomas Hendrik Ilves and Algirdas Saudargas. The ministers also announced that the two countries would coordinate their NATO policy.
- Ex-banker Rein Kaarepere accused the state of having caused the failure of his Tartu Commercial Bank (TKP) in 1992. Kaarepere is charged with negligence and abuse of his position.

- The State Court will decide on the oath of office of President Lennart Meri on February 20. The validity of the oath has been questioned by three politicians that Meri had been connected with the KGB Soviet secret police.
- The Internet guestbook of Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi had to be closed due to numerous obscene entries.
- The former military plant Dvigatel hopes that the meeting of the French and Estonian presidents this week will give political approval to missile component production.

- Two Estonian diplomats told the daily that the EU has decided that the failure to conclude an Estonian-Russian border agreement will no longer be considered as an obstruction to the possible admission of Estonia to the EU.
- The Rural Union stated that a sacking the agriculture minister would be made in late March only.
- Sales of shares push up privatisation voucher prices.
- Tallinna Pank says the TH Ferries shipping firm has made loans worth 50 million kroons besides the bank's 41 million kroon loan.
